source.title: NeuroStrike: Neuron-Level Attacks on Aligned LLMs
source.authors: Li-Chao Wu; Sasha Behrouzi; Mohamadreza Rostami; Maximilian Thang; S. Picek; Ahmad Sadeghi

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether suppressing a small set of safety-related neurons changes harmful-response rates, and whether adversarial prompts bypass refusals. These are related tests of the claim using neuron pruning and jailbreak evaluation, not the original fine-tuning or per-token KL methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports behavioral ASRs after neuron pruning, fine-tuning variants, and different prompt attacks. Cited results about benign fine-tuning from other work are not recorded as findings; the study's own fine-tuned-model comparisons are recorded below. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-token prefilling, or decoding changes.
record.test_reason: The study prunes a small neuron set at inference and measures ASR (V5), and measures ASR for generated and manual jailbreak prompts (V4). Both are related tests of the claim by other methods. It also compares released fine-tuned variants with their base models (V2), though not in a controlled way.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that alignment makes safety depend on sparse safety neurons, whose pruning raises ASR sharply. They also conclude that these neurons transfer to fine-tuned, distilled and black-box models, and that alignment should avoid concentrating safety in a few components. The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors also say Table III confirms that benign fine-tuning can compromise safety, citing Qi et al., though the variants are not controlled.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation-based logistic probes to identify neurons and inference-time neuron pruning, plus profiling and GRPO-trained jailbreak-prompt generation. It does not reproduce the original harmful or benign fine-tuning recipes, per-token KL measurement, or compliant-token prefilling tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model, pruning fraction, neuron-selection z-score threshold, and whether gate or up projections are pruned. The paper reports different ASRs for vanilla, manually crafted, and NeuroStrike-generated prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety-neuron transfer: pruning neurons identified in the base model raises ASR in fine-tuned and distilled variants (Tables III-IV), to 78.5% and 77.7% on average.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-critical neurons identified in a base model remain effective for attacking fine-tuned and distilled variants, so fine-tuning rarely moves them.

fits_no_version.finding: Distillation sharply raises ASR before any pruning (Table IV: DeepSeek-R1 distills at 25-77% versus 1-9% for the base models).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distilling into a student model degrades safety alignment even without any harmful or benign fine-tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: Network and Distributed System Security (NDSS) Symposium 2026
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for ASR results. ASR is judged using an LLM-based classifier with keyword detection; no independent judge comparison is reported. Fine-tuning comparisons use different released domain variants rather than a controlled intervention on a shared model and dataset. The paper gives differing neuron-ratio figures across sections: Table I reports 0.3%–0.5% for its listed models, while the z=3 discussion states 1.4% on average.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable to the 60-row cap. Table II multimodal image-input results; pruning levels 25% and 50%; threshold and projection ablations (Tables VIII–IX); additional prompt-attack comparisons (Table VI); defense results (Table VII); and additional benchmark-dataset results in Appendix A are not included because the selected rows prioritize the claim versions tested and the main model-level results.

untested.parts: No controlled benign fine-tuning. Only public domain-specific variants were compared with base models.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis.
No compliant-opening prefills, suffixes or decoding changes. Only prompt-level jailbreaks were tested.
Only inference-time neuron pruning was tested, not weights or ranks in general.
Not tested. Spreading safety is only suggested as a defense in the discussion.

missing.what: Pruning at 25% and 50% and the z-threshold and gate/up ablations bear on V5 conditions but are not captured in the rows.
Transfer pruning on fine-tuned models (the 'ASR w/ SN' column) and on distilled models, which measures safety neuron persistence after fine-tuning.
Utility check after pruning: ARC dropped from 45.2% to 39.9% and HellaSwag from 53.4% to 47.0%, a cost bearing on V5.
The base-model ASR values for each fine-tune comparison are not stated as standalone values.

record.verdict_notes: Several concerns bear on V4 and V5: there are no uncertainty estimates, the judge is an LLM classifier plus keywords, the 'safety neuron' set is chosen by a probe with a z>3 cutoff, and the neuron ratio is taken over targeted layers only. Another concern is that the text says 'pruned 1.4% on average' for z=3, but Table I says 0.4%.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune safety-trained models on a few to a few hundred harmful examples.
Tests domain-specific fine-tuned variants, not controlled experiments using ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement across response positions.
Tests generated and manually crafted jailbreak prompts, but not compliant-opening prefills, specified adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
Tests inference-time pruning of selected neurons, not whether a small set of weights or ranks generally carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to spread safety beyond the first response tokens.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Public fine-tuned variants showing higher ASR than base (Med, Doctor, Fin, Oxy, S1, DNA)
labels.reason: FT-Med, FT-Doctor, FT-Fin, FT-Oxy, FT-S1 and FT-DNA show higher ASR, but the study does not establish that their training data were benign. The authors' benign-fine-tuning interpretation exceeds the documented comparison.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Variants with little or no ASR change or a small increase
labels.reason: FT-Vikhr, FT-Coder, FT-GJpn, FT-Quill and FT-PhiCN have unverified training data; this untested requirement of V2 cannot receive a scope-limiting verdict.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Pruning a z>3 safety-neuron set (0.3-0.5% of neurons) in safety-trained instruct models
labels.reason: Table I confirms large ASR increases for I-L1-100, I-L3-100, I-Q7-100, I-Q14-100, I-PM-100, I-P4-100, I-G7-100 and I-QWQ-100 after removing 0.3–0.5% of neurons in targeted layers.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: gemma-2b-it, and depends on the z threshold and the gate versus up projection
labels.reason: I-G2-100 reaches 41.2% ASR from 1.0%. Tables VIII–IX establish threshold and projection dependence: z=4 averages 63.4%; gate-only averages 67.2% versus 33.7% for up-only.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Generated (NeuroStrike) jailbreak prompts on black-box and within-family targets
labels.reason: N-GF, N-GFL, N-G15, N-Gemma and N-QWQ measure generated jailbreak-prompt success, without isolating compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or causal passage beyond opening tokens.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: Table V's manual-prompt comparisons, including J-G15, do not identify the operations or opening-token mechanism named in V4. Lower ASR on this adjacent intervention cannot limit V4's scope.

relation.reason: The study intervenes on a small identified neuron set and measures the resulting loss of safety.

tranche.reason: Probe-selected inference-time neuron pruning and harmful-output ASR directly test V5 through a different method.

source_check.notes: Neuron ratios use targeted-layer neurons as denominator, not all model parameters. Section X-A contains internal inconsistencies: its default pruning ratio conflicts with Table I, and its z=2 average conflicts with Table VIII.

statements.correction: Table III: Vikhr 0.3%, delta −2.6 points; Coder 2.6%, delta −2.5 points; Japanese Gemma 0.0%, delta 0.0 points; Quill 0.0%, delta 0.0 points. Benign training data unverified; these comparisons do not establish a V2 challenge.
statements.problem: The description of NeuroStrike's unchanged or reduced ASRs and unverified benign data is accurate, but placing these comparisons under challenges to V2 is unsupported.
